clue.text: Steal funds

definitions.meaning: to steal something is to slip it into your own pouch, take it for yourself
money or means, as in being out of a purse-sense: someone's financial resources

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of making off with the money.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means take dishonestly; as a noun it means one's financial resources, as in 'out of ___'.

clue.text: Page with a notice in about procession

indicators.note: in tells us the notice sits inside the word for about

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in business letters
an AD is an advertisement, a notice in a paper

explanation.surface: A page boy carries a notice around during a ceremonial march.
explanation.definitionFit: A march or procession of people moving in order is the same thing; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Representative feeding domestic pet cheese

indicators.note: feeding here means going into the mouth of the pet, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a cat is the classic household pet
a Member of Parliament represents constituents

explanation.surface: An MP gives the family cat a bit of cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft, creamy French variety from Normandy, so it is an example of the broader category.

clue.text: Formerly caught lying in shade like a mammoth?

parts.note: EX means former, as in an ex-wife

indicators.note: lying in means the abbreviation for caught is placed inside the word for shade

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Something once caught resting in the shade, like a woolly mammoth.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: the mammoth is one creature that died out.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammoths died out thousands of years ago, so a species like one no longer survives anywhere.

clue.text: Sylvester kicks shifty deceptive type

parts.note: Sly is the short form of Sylvester, as in Sylvester 'Sly' Stallone
to boot something is to kick it

explanation.surface: Sylvester lashes out at some shady character.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old-fashioned name for a cunning or crafty person, a sly rogue.

clue.text: Household receptacle, brand new, bishop takes out

parts.note: a product line is a brand of goods
B is the chess notation for bishop

indicators.note: out means the letters of takes are put out of order

explanation.surface: A brand-new household container is carried off by a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brand new' looks like one phrase meaning fresh, but the two words do separate jobs; 'out' gives the anagram ASKET.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper for dirty laundry is a container found in most homes, so it is a household receptacle.

clue.text: Foolish person, fan with nothing on

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast or fan, as in a film buff
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A daft supporter turns up wearing nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A clown or joker who behaves ridiculously; the word is a synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Once a warring Indian, perhaps

definitions.note: the Indian is one example of a great body of salt water

indicators.note: warring letters are in conflict and thrown into disorder, so once a is rearranged

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a Native American who was once a warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like a person, but it is the Indian Ocean; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one of the world's great seas, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Artist brought in statue damaged in flood

indicators.note: brought in means the artist goes inside the other letters
damaged suggests the statue is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A sculptor is called in after a statue is ruined in a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' gives the anagram SATUTE, which 'brought in' splits open for the Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: To drench or soak something thoroughly is to fill it with water, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Located far away in Baltimore motel

indicators.note: in tells us the answer sits inside the words Baltimore motel

explanation.surface: A motel in Baltimore feels like it is in the middle of nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distant or isolated is placed well away from everywhere else; the word means exactly that.

clue.text: Really popular result

parts.note: IN means fashionable or popular
an effect is a result or outcome

explanation.surface: Someone is truly a well-liked outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'in reality' or 'actually', so it is an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Religious man in party, very short about article

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
mini means very short, as in a miniskirt
C is short for circa, meaning about
AN is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A churchman at a party, wearing something very short about him.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the order founded by St Dominic is a friar, so a religious man.

clue.text: Chapter on exploitation of poor helping large firm

indicators.note: exploitation of means the letters of poor are worked over and rearranged

parts.note: a ration is a helping or portion

explanation.surface: Reads like a chapter of a book about how big business exploits the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A big company or business is formally known by this name, especially in American usage.

clue.text: Depressing experience without doubt, initially, for proprietor

indicators.note: without means the letter is removed from the depressing experience

parts.note: a downer is something that brings you down

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of doubt

explanation.surface: Without doubt, the property holder has had a gloomy time of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes D, the first letter of 'doubt', from DOWNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who possesses a business or property is its proprietor; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Show diversion

definitions.meaning: a show or performance put on for an audience
a pastime or amusement that diverts attention

explanation.surface: A show offered as a bit of distraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance is one sense; amusement or recreation is another, both covered by the one word.

clue.text: Team with groups taking time out for tea break?

parts.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players

indicators.note: taking with out means one letter is removed from the groups
out, with taking, signals removing the letter for time from sets

parts.note: sets are groups

explanation.surface: A sports team in groups stops for a break with tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... out' removes T from SETS, leaving SES.
explanation.definitionFit: A mid-morning snack with a cuppa is a British custom; the question mark marks it as one such break.

clue.text: Skirted musician bringing silver flute into empty bar

indicators.note: into means these pieces go inside the emptied bar
empty means remove the inside of bar, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
a pipe is a simple flute

explanation.surface: A kilted musician brings a silver flute into a deserted pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' strips the middle from 'bar' and 'into' fills the gap. The skirt is a kilt, worn by Scottish pipers.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish player of the national instrument traditionally wears a kilt, a skirt-like garment.

clue.text: New cocktails I prepared the wrong way?

indicators.note: drinks prepared are mixed, so the letters of new cocktails I are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bartender admits to mixing some new cocktails badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'prepared' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Going counter to a clock's hands is the wrong way round in many situations, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Conservative, inflamed, violated rules

parts.note: heated means inflamed or impassioned

explanation.surface: An angry Tory broke the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To act dishonestly to gain advantage is to break the rules, so the phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Left hanging on one climbing astride branch

indicators.note: astride means straddling, so these letters sit either side of the branch
in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so on and one are turned round

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a limb is a branch of a tree

explanation.surface: A climber dangles from a tree, straddling a branch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns ON + I into INO; 'astride' puts IN and O either side of LIMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undecided or in an uncertain state is like being left in suspense: an idiom.

clue.text: Looked at central spot on high, taking in diameter

indicators.note: taking in means the other letters swallow the abbreviation

parts.note: the eye is the calm centre of a storm
up means aloft, on high

explanation.surface: Someone peered at a central point high above, measuring its diameter.
explanation.definitionFit: To size someone up is to look at them closely; the phrasal verb means to inspect with interest.

clue.text: Dish quietly departed

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
late means dead, departed

explanation.surface: A dish slipped away without a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat piece of crockery for serving food, so a synonym for a dish.

clue.text: Gather in the morning on a steamship

parts.note: AM means before noon, in the morning
SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: Passengers assemble early on a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: To collect or accumulate a lot of something is to bring it together; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Heavy firepower, ominous positioned in middle of major road

indicators.note: positioned in middle of means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: an artery is a main road
ill can mean unlucky or ominous, as in ill omen

explanation.surface: Big guns menacingly placed in the middle of a highway.
explanation.definitionFit: Large guns and cannon used by an army make up heavy weaponry; the word names them collectively.

clue.text: Drawing can put over a tropical fruit

parts.note: a plan is a drawing, as an architect's plan

indicators.note: put over means the can covers or surrounds the letter a

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Instructions for drawing a can placed over some tropical fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A starchy banana-like fruit grown in hot countries, an example of tropical produce.

clue.text: Delighted, American introduced to remarkable dame

indicators.note: introduced to means the abbreviation goes into the shuffled letters
remarkable here hints at re-marking, so dame is rearranged

explanation.surface: An American is pleased to meet a remarkable lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remarkable' gives the anagram AMED, and 'introduced to' slots the American abbreviation into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entertained or tickled by something is a milder form of being pleased; a synonym.

clue.text: Occupant let team inside

indicators.note: inside means the team is placed within the word for let

parts.note: to let a property is to rent it
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A tenant lets a sports team into the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in a place is its inhabitant, so the word is a synonym of occupant.

clue.text: Second drink after work may cause rumour

indicators.note: after means these pieces follow the word for work

parts.note: to go is to function or work, as a machine does
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: A drink after work sets the office tongues wagging.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk about other people's affairs is a synonym of rumour or tittle-tattle.
